findings.message: Rows are indexed by column name, which only works when the caller has set `connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row`; with a default connection, `row["id"]` raises `TypeError` because rows are plain tuples. The function's signature accepts any `sqlite3.Connection`, so this precondition is hidden.

User-controlled email and name values are written unescaped to a file meant to be opened in a spreadsheet. A name starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is evaluated as a formula when support staff open the file (CSV/formula injection).
The test creates a single user, so it cannot show that users are written in id order. The criterion requires a test that proves the ordering, for example by inserting several users out of order.

criteria.note: The query orders by id, but no test proves the order: the only test inserts a single user.
